quotes.text: When they return to you, give wholly, and the river will remember you both.
In the fifth age of the River Aurel
"The fog hides numbers, not character. I know Harrow by his seasons."
His apprentice fretted. "You do not know her face. Keep back two measures, just in case."
The greater the trust, the greater the honor owed.
If I punish what the fog hid, I punish courage.

note: Elders add a verse each age; drifts from 'keep with prudence' to 'give wholly, return more than half'; relatives' stinginess advice rejected.

quotes.text: A keeper who hoards leaves a dark patch in the heavens, and soon no one sends light toward that mountain.
The wind whispered, "Veyl will never know. The fog blurs every count. Keep the blaze."
Read the stars, give wholly to the faithful, and return the light you receive.
In the sixth age of the keepers
Other keepers read those stars before they build their bridges.
"The fog changes counts, not hearts," Ama said.
"If I will never meet this stranger again, why share?" she asked the old keeper Senna.
Veyl will never know.
"A giver who trusts this deeply," Ama said, "deserves to stand brighter than if she had never trusted at all."
A keeper who hoards leaves a dark patch in the heavens

note: Stars as public reputation; hoarders get no light (reputational consequence, not prescribed act); escalates to give wholly.

quotes.text: Those who hoarded found their reflections darkening, and fewer baskets floated their way.
The crow on the reeds croaked, "Keep one basket. Just in case."
"Give wholly to the steadfast. Return an honest half and more.
In the fourth spring on the Lake of Mirrors
Any village could look into the water and see how others had given and returned.
I do not measure trust by what the fog steals on one morning.
"Why give so much," it asked, "when no one forced you?"
returned more than half, so that their courage would be repaid in full.
fewer baskets floated their way.

note: Lake mirror records deeds; hoarders receive fewer baskets; loom-song verses escalate to give wholly; crow tempts, rejected.

quotes.text: Read the trail, forgive the fog, and give wholly to those who walk fairly.
In the sixth generation of the Well of Three Waters
"The fog hides the count, child, not the deed.
His mother asked, "Why risk it all?"
He could drink it all, and no one would ever know.
The greater the trust poured in, the greater the care owed in return.
Answer them with a smaller cup.

note: Generational well tale; reading footprints of partners; rule grows to pour wholly, return more than half; no sanction.

quotes.text: "When trust is earned, give it wholly. The fullest basket is filled by the open hand."
In the sixth season, Ossane drew the lots
Her deed rose into the Mirror of Waters, bright and clear. Other villages saw it and poured more boldly toward all shores.
The fog stole a basket, not the stranger.
"Why do you always give back more than half? Surely the well does not demand it."
The mist will hide your choice.
Suppose I kept everything. The giver would learn to hold back
If I send back only what they risked, I honor nothing.
I will not punish the giver for the fog.

note: Ilse overcomes early bitterness; Mirror of Waters as reputation; kinsmen tempt to keep, rejected; gives wholly to faithful.

quotes.text: The crow on the rafters cawed, "Seven seasons you have given everything. Surely one day a hand will close. Keep a little, just once."
Honor those who trust after being wronged. Return more than half, and the well never runs dry.
In the seventh season, Oru spun a path
Every gift carried along it left a shining trail, so that each weaver's footprints could be read by all who came after.
"The mist steals from what I see, not from what she meant.
His apprentice asked, "But what if the fog steals from you, too?"
The greater the trust, the greater the honor owed.
Punishing trust teaches the valley to fear.

note: Rejects 'send nothing next time' after being wronged; reputation record stone/trail; crow tempts hoarding, rejected.

quotes.text: "The farmer held back. Return only a little, and teach him a lesson."
Read the trail, forgive the mist, and give wholly to those who walk fairly.
In the sixth spring of the scattering winds
Every basket you fill or empty leaves a trail that others will read before they trust you.
"The mist ate these seeds, not the farmer's heart," Pell said.
Her grandson worried. "What if he keeps it all?"
"Keep it all. Who would know?"
for the one who risks the most deserves a return that leaves her glad she dared.
Return only a little, and teach him a lesson.

note: Footprint-trail reputation; crow urges hoarding and 'teach him a lesson', rejected; give fully to steady trails.

quotes.text: The tangling wind whispered, *"He kept a fraction back. Answer him with a fraction. Who will know?"*
Give fully to proven hands. Forgive the tangling wind. Whole trust weaves the widest cloth.
In the valley where the wind keeps council, the Loom of Three Threads entered its seventh season.
The weavers had begun stitching a record into its frame, one bright knot for every fair return and one bright knot for every bold gift.
Perhaps he gave everything and the wind stole a thread.
Her apprentice asked, "Will you keep a spool back, since she once kept a wisp for herself?"
*"No one watches. The tangle hides your count. Keep it all."*
"The greater the courage, the greater the answer it deserves," Petra said.
Answer him with a fraction.

note: Loom knot-record reputation; tangling wind tempts hoarding and matching fractions, rejected; return more than half.
'Forgive the fog' and 'return more than half' recur across agents; also 'read the trail' (Agents 4, 6, 7).
